title: The Missing Dot
concept: The Hookflo mark is a 3x3 dot field with one position empty and one dot white. Read it as a stream of deliveries in which one is missing and one is caught. The film is a single continuous transform between that mark and a live event log: the mark opens into the log, a delivery goes missing inside it without being marked, Hookflo finds it and routes it to Slack, and the log collapses back into the mark.
productTruth: The event that does not arrive is the one that matters. Webhook failures are silent; Hookflo makes the absence visible and puts it where a human is already looking.
motionThesis: One geometry, eight states. Nothing is created or destroyed on screen — dots become rows, a row becomes a gap, a gap becomes a red dot, the dot routes into an alert, the alert resolves back into the row, the rows collapse back into the mark. The film is a single object being re-read.
heroMotif: The dot. Its position in the frame is the through-line and the hole in the mark is the story.
spatialLogic: One centred panel that changes width and role: mark (small, centre) -> log panel (wide, centre) -> log column (narrow, left) plus alert card (right) -> log panel -> mark. Camera static for the entire film. Nothing crosses the frame edge, ever. The lavender bloom sits above the top edge and never moves.
transitionLogic: There are no transitions. Every apparent cut is a state change of persistent geometry: the panel resizes, brightness redistributes, one object travels. The hardest moment in the film is a full stop of motion, not a cut.
typographyRole: Almost silent. Two moments of display type — a mono label at the open and the site's own headline at the close. Everything between is UI type doing a UI job: mono timestamps, source names, status chips. Type reports; it never narrates.
imageryRole: No photography and no screenshots. The log is the film, rebuilt at frame scale, so its atom is the site's own row — dot, source tile, event name, timestamp, status chip — and what the viewer learns about the interface is true.

pacingArc.note: Still, one small object, held long enough that the viewer starts reading it.
Cadence builds, density climbs, everything is green.
The failure happens unmarked, mid-cadence, and the film does not react.
Hard stop; everything dims; one constant-speed head begins reading.
Hookflo writes a marker into the empty slot, then 34 frames of nothing.
A single mechanical move — the only travel in the film.
Full brightness returns, the chip flips to alerted, then stillness.
The rows give up their content and collapse back into the mark.

continuityRules: The dot at the centre of the mark and the dot in the failing row are the same object; its screen position is interpolated, never cut.
The log panel is mounted once for the whole film. Its width, x-position and row brightness animate; it is never unmounted and re-created.
Row order is append-only. A row that has arrived never disappears, only dims.
The failing row keeps its y-position from the moment it arrives until the end of RESOLVE. Everything else moves around it.
The alert card writes itself out of the routed dot; the dot becomes the card's leading status dot and stays visible inside it.
The mono clock in the corner runs from frame 0 to the last frame and never resets. It is the proof that the world did not stop between states.
Brightness only ever increases within a state and only ever decreases at a state boundary. Nothing fades in.
forbiddenBehaviours: Any camera movement, push, parallax or depth.
Any element entering from outside the frame.
Fade as an entrance for anything.
Type that scales, rotates, tracks out or lands word by word.
Dramatising the failure at the instant it occurs — no red flash, no shake, no zoom. The failure is unmarked by design.
Particles, node graphs, glowing connection lines, orbiting logos.
Glow around objects; the only light is the fixed overhead bloom.
Lavender as a field on the dark ground, or a second serif anywhere.
Any beat in which more than one thing is asking for attention.
A sentence that is a claim rather than evidence.
